Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2) — a from-scratch visual/UX redesign ("Nexion") of a hosting platform's customer dashboard, built on a real backend. This is a READ-ONLY audit before production promotion — do not edit or fix anything, only report findings with file:line evidence.

A prior audit already confirmed (background only, don't re-check): app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx correctly computes click/conversion counts from real `db.referralClick` queries, BUT no code anywhere ever WRITES a `ReferralClick` row — so referral click tracking is permanently stuck at 0 clicks for every user. Also confirmed: `Partner.type` field has zero admin UI to set it (admin-side gap, already covered, don't re-check admin side).

Your job — audit the rest of the CUSTOMER-FACING referral/affiliate experience: app/dashboard/refer and app/dashboard/affiliate (both exist per the dashboard nav — find both, they may be the same feature under two labels or genuinely separate features, figure out which).

Check and report on:
1. **Referral reward/credit**: when someone signs up using a referral code, does the referrer actually receive a real credit (search for `signupCreditCents`, `referredById` usage in lib/actions.ts or similar) — is this a real, correctly-computed wallet credit, or does the referral dashboard just show an aspirational "you'll earn $X" with nothing actually crediting?
2. **Affiliate program** (if genuinely distinct from "refer a friend" — e.g. a formal Partner/affiliate program with commission tracking): is there a real signup/application flow for a customer to BECOME an affiliate, and if so does it create a real `ReferralPartner`/`Partner`-type row? Is commission tracked and paid out via any real mechanism, or is it UI-only?
3. **Referral link/code generation**: does every customer get a real, unique `referralCode` (schema field on User) that's actually generated and displayed correctly, and does the shareable link actually work end-to-end (visiting it as a new user and registering actually attributes the signup, per `lib/actions.ts:203`'s `referredById` set from a cookie)?
4. **Any UI element that shows a number/stat that isn't backed by a real query** — e.g. a "total earned" or "friends referred" stat that might be hardcoded or use fake math instead of a real aggregate.
5. **Security**: can a customer manipulate their own referral code or another user's via any client-controlled input, or is code generation/lookup fully server-controlled?

Report as a table: Feature | REAL / PARTIAL / STUB | evidence (file:line) | what's missing. Keep under 600 words. Do not modify any files.

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - **Do not** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Referral / Affiliate Audit — Customer-Facing (app/dashboard/refer, app/dashboard/affiliate, app/dashboard/partner)

**Structure**: `/dashboard/affiliate` is a pure redirect (`app/dashboard/affiliate/page.tsx:9`) to `/dashboard/refer` — same feature, not two features. `/dashboard/partner` (`app/dashboard/partner/page.tsx`) is a genuinely separate, admin-provisioned agency/KOL program using `ReferralPartner`/`PartnerCustomer`/`PartnerCommission`.

| # | Feature | Status | Evidence | What's missing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Referral reward crediting | **REAL** | `lib/actions-growth.ts:466-516` `maybeRewardReferral()` — gated by `hasPaidAction()` precondition (line 474), atomic claim via `updateMany` on `referralRewardedAt` (497-500), then a real `$transaction` incrementing `balanceCents` for both referrer and referred user + `WalletTransaction` rows (503-516). Called from real money paths: `lib/order.ts:1019`, `lib/stripe.ts:1473`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:680`, `lib/actions.ts:939`. | Nothing — this is a real, defended (anti-farming) credit. |
| 2 | Affiliate/partner application flow | **STUB (customer-facing)** | `lib/actions-partner.ts:29-71` `adminCreatePartner()` requires `requireArea("billing")` — admin-only. No customer-side "become a partner/affiliate" form found anywhere in `app/dashboard` or `components/nx/PartnerView.tsx`. | No self-serve signup; a customer can only become a partner if an admin manually creates the `ReferralPartner` row via `linkEmail`. Commission tracking/payout itself (`PartnerCommission`, `computePartnerSummary` in `lib/partner-commission.ts`) is real once attached. |
| 3a | Referral code generation | **REAL** | `app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx:24-37` `ensureReferralCode()` — lazily generates via `generateReferralCode()` (`lib/growth.ts:32`), checks DB uniqueness, retries on race, persists to `User.referralCode`. | None. |
| 3b | Shareable link end-to-end | **STUB** | `app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx:91`: link shown to the customer is `${APP_URL}/r/${code}`. No `app/r/` route exists anywhere in the tree, no rewrite in `next.config.ts` (only unrelated 301s for blog/marketing), no `/r` handling in `middleware.ts`. `app/go/[slug]/route.ts` is an unrelated ad-campaign redirector. Contrast: the partner portal correctly links to `${appUrl}/register?ref=${partner.code}` (`app/dashboard/partner/page.tsx:65`), and `ReferralCapture` (`components/customer/ReferralCapture.tsx`) only reads `?ref=` on the `/register` page itself. | The customer's own referral link 404s in production — visiting it never reaches `/register`, never sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie, so a genuine referred signup via that link is never attributed at all (compounding the already-known click-tracking gap). |
| 4 | Stats/UI numbers | **REAL** | All figures in `RewardsView` are backed by real aggregates: `total`/`rewarded`/`thisMonth`/`lastMonth` (`app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx:49-52`), `earnedCents = rewarded * rewardCents` (105), `pendingCents` (106), monthly sparkline series built from real `createdAt`/`referralRewardedAt` rows (68-86), zero-filled rather than invented. `clicks`/`convertedClicks` are real queries (55-56) but — per prior audit — always 0 since nothing writes `ReferralClick`. | Only the pre-known click/conversion-rate gap; no other hardcoded/fake numbers found. |
| 5 | Security — code manipulation | **REAL (safe)** | `ensureReferralCode` never accepts client input, only generates/persists server-side (item 3a). `ReferralCapture` (`components/customer/ReferralCapture.tsx:14-20`) lets a client set an arbitrary `nxeon_ref` cookie, but `lib/actions.ts:203-219` only honors it if it matches a real, existing `User.referralCode` or `ReferralPartner.code` via server-side `findUnique` — self-referral is structurally impossible (brand-new account), and no endpoint lets a user set/overwrite their own or another's `referralCode`/`referredById`. | None found. |

Bottom line: the reward math and payout are solid, but the customer's own share link is dead code (`/r/{code}` has no route) — a separate, more actionable bug than the already-known missing click-write, since it also breaks conversion attribution end-to-end for anyone using the link as displayed. The "affiliate program" is not a distinct customer feature; it's a UI redirect to `/refer`, and becoming a commission-earning *partner* has no customer application path at all today.
